platform.name: Example multi-asset platform
platform.description: Example scope showing both supported web target forms: an absolute service URL and asset host/IP plus service port/protocol/base path.

authorization.reference: Replace with the real authorization/ticket/reference and set confirmed=true before executing a real assessment. This example enables discovered same-host HTTP/HTTPS multi-port scope.

portal_user.purpose: Ordinary user identity. Cookie is tried first; if the environment does not provide a usable session or username/password, assessmentRunner asks once in the console for this identity.

portal_editor.purpose: Second account/role. Missing environment credentials are prompted independently, so authorization/BOLA checks can compare this identity with the others.

portal_admin.purpose: Higher-privilege example identity. It becomes a separate authenticated profile; scanners run with its own session rather than merging credentials.

services.notes: Absolute-URL form. Three configured identities become distinct authenticated profiles, in addition to anonymous because auth_only=false. If their env vars are missing, the runner prompts once per identity. Authorization/BOLA compares the active identity with every other available identity.
Host/IP + port form. This service resolves from asset.host plus port/protocol/base_path; omitting protocol would infer HTTP for port 80.
Host/IP + port form with explicit HTTPS. Each configured identity is resolved independently for this service; same-host/OIDC reuse remains subject to the authorization and issuer/realm safeguards.
The service is part of the platform inventory; the current web orchestrators record it as unsupported and do not test it.
